title: Illumina Spatial Transcriptomics Technical Framework
author: Shuoshuo Wang
materials: The Illumina spatial transcriptomics assay is designed to address these limitations. By utilizing proprietary flow cell manufacturing and surface chemistry, the platform introduces a continuous capture substrate featuring 1-micrometer structural resolution, paired with unbiased polyadenylated (polyA) transcript capture. This framework utilizes high-throughput sequencing, specifically on platforms such as the NovaSeq X Series, with machine learning-based cell segmentation and cloud-based tertiary analysis pipelines. The resulting ecosystem allows for the simultaneous mapping of individual cells across large tissue sections while maintaining transcriptomic depth and spatial fidelity. The Illumina platform’s 50 × 15 mm footprint is designed to accommodate intact tissue sections, such as whole murine organs or multi-tissue microarrays. This area reduces the bioinformatics requirement of computationally stitching multiple disparate sequencing runs together, a process that can introduce batch effects, edge artifacts, and alignment errors. Furthermore, the 1-micrometer feature size allows distinct spatial barcodes to fall within the physical boundary of a single mammalian cell (which typically ranges from 5 to 10 micrometers in diameter). This dense functionalization minimizes the artificial mixing of transcripts from adjacent cells, allowing downstream bioinformatics algorithms to assign captured mRNA to discrete, individual cells.

steps.title: Collect and Fresh‑Freeze Tissue
steps.instruction: Harvest tissue rapidly, embed it in Optimal Cutting Temperature (OCT) compound, snap‑freeze the OCT block in an isopentane bath chilled with liquid nitrogen, and keep the frozen block on dry ice until sectioning.

substeps.instruction: Embed tissue in OCT.
Snap‑freeze in isopentane chilled with liquid nitrogen.
Store frozen block on dry ice.

steps.title: Cryosection and Place on Slide
steps.instruction: Mount the OCT‑embedded block in a cryostat, set the internal temperature to –15 °C – –25 °C (adjust for tissue lipid content), cut 10 µm sections, and transfer each section onto the 50 × 15 mm active capture area of the Illumina spatial slide (75 × 25 mm slide, 7.5 cm² active area) ensuring the tissue lies flat without folds, tears, or trapped air bubbles.

substeps.instruction: Mount block in cryostat.
Set temperature to –15 °C – –25 °C.
Cut 10 µm sections.
Transfer section onto the 50 × 15 mm capture area.
Flatten tissue to eliminate bubbles and folds.

steps.title: Fix Tissue with Cold Methanol
steps.instruction: Immerse the slide‑mounted section in cold methanol to fix morphology and inhibit RNase activity.

steps.title: H&E Stain Tissue
steps.instruction: Perform standard Hematoxylin and Eosin staining: hematoxylin stains acidic nucleic acids in nuclei blue/purple, eosin stains basic cytoplasmic and extracellular matrix proteins pink.

substeps.instruction: Apply hematoxylin stain.
Rinse.
Apply eosin counter‑stain.
Rinse and dry.

steps.title: Image H&E and Fiducial Markers
steps.instruction: Capture a bright‑field multi‑tile image of the entire 50 × 15 mm tissue area, including the etched fiducial markers on the glass, to create the spatial reference map for downstream analysis.

substeps.instruction: Set up bright‑field microscope.
Acquire tiled images covering the whole capture area.
Save image file with fiducial marker positions.

steps.title: Permeabilize Tissue
steps.instruction: Apply a permeabilization enzyme mix containing pepsin or proteinase K together with detergents, incubate for the tissue‑specific optimal time (avoid under‑ or over‑permeabilization), then wash to remove excess enzyme.

substeps.instruction: Prepare enzyme mix (pepsin or proteinase K + detergents).
Apply mix to the section.
Incubate for the optimized duration.
Wash slide to stop the reaction.

steps.title: Reverse Transcribe Captured mRNA
steps.instruction: Add reverse transcriptase enzyme to the slide so that it synthesizes cDNA from the surface‑bound poly‑A mRNA using the spatial capture probe as primer, thereby attaching the spatial barcode and UMI to the newly formed cDNA.

substeps.instruction: Prepare reverse transcription (RT) mix.
Apply RT mix to the slide.
Incubate at the RT temperature for the recommended time.
Wash to remove enzymes.

steps.title: Release Surface‑Bound cDNA
steps.instruction: Digest remaining tissue, then release the spatially barcoded cDNA either by enzymatic cleavage at the engineered restriction site or by alkaline denaturation, and collect the eluate containing the cDNA.

substeps.instruction: Biochemically digest tissue remnants.
Choose release method: restriction enzyme cleavage OR alkaline denaturation.
Perform release reaction.
Collect eluate with released cDNA.

steps.title: Amplify cDNA by PCR
steps.instruction: Perform PCR amplification using primers that target the universal sequences added during the template‑switching oligo (TSO) phase, generating sufficient material for library preparation.

substeps.instruction: Set up PCR with universal primers.
Run appropriate number of cycles.
Purify amplified cDNA.

steps.title: Prepare Sequencing Library
steps.instruction: Fragment the amplified cDNA to a size appropriate for Illumina platforms, then ligate standard Illumina adapters (P5 and P7) and sample multiplexing indices (i5 and i7) to produce a dual‑indexed library that contains the transcript sequence, UMI, and spatial barcode.

substeps.instruction: Fragment cDNA to the desired size range.
Perform size selection.
Ligate P5/P7 adapters and i5/i7 indices.
Cleanup and quantify the final library.

steps.title: Sequence Library on Illumina Platform
steps.instruction: Load the dual‑indexed library onto a high‑throughput Illumina sequencer (e.g., NovaSeq 6000 or NovaSeq X) and run a paired‑end read with the custom read structure required to capture spatial barcode, UMI, and transcript reads.

substeps.instruction: Denature and dilute library to the recommended loading concentration.
Load onto NovaSeq flow cell.
Execute a dual‑indexed paired‑end run with the custom cycle allocation.

steps.title: Convert BCL to FASTQ
steps.instruction: Convert the unaligned BCL files generated by the sequencer into FASTQ files for downstream processing.

substeps.instruction: Run bcl2fastq (or equivalent) to produce FASTQ files.

steps.title: Align Reads and Decode Spatial Information
steps.instruction: Use the DRAGEN spatial pipeline to align Read 2 (biological transcript) to the reference genome, decode Read 1 for spatial barcode and UMI, and merge the streams so each transcript is assigned its physical coordinate on the slide.

substeps.instruction: Align Read 2 with splice‑aware RNA mapper.
Extract spatial barcode and UMI from Read 1.
Combine alignment and barcode data.

steps.title: Deduplicate UMIs
steps.instruction: Within the DRAGEN pipeline, collapse reads that share identical genomic locus, spatial barcode, and UMI into a single count to remove PCR duplicates.

steps.title: Register Image and Segment Cells
steps.instruction: Run the Spatial Image Aligner to register the bright‑field H&E image with the fiducial markers, then apply the machine‑learning cell‑segmentation model (nucleus detection via hematoxylin stain followed by border expansion) to generate cellular polygons and assign spatial barcodes to each cell.

substeps.instruction: Import H&E image and detect fiducial markers.
Create affine registration map.
Execute ML‑based nucleus detection.
Expand nuclei to estimate cell borders.
Generate cell polygons linked to spatial barcodes.

steps.title: Generate Cell‑by‑Gene Expression Matrix
steps.instruction: Aggregate transcripts that fall within each cellular polygon to produce a matrix of gene counts per segmented cell.

substeps.instruction: Bin spatial barcodes to cells.
Count unique UMIs per gene per cell.

steps.title: Perform Downstream Analysis in ICM
steps.instruction: Import the expression matrix into Illumina Connected Multiomics (ICM) for visualization, dimensionality reduction, Leiden clustering, spatial differential expression, and optional multi‑omic integration.

substeps.instruction: Load matrix into ICM.
Create spatial heatmaps and plots.
Run dimensionality reduction (e.g., UMAP).
Apply Leiden clustering to define cell types.
Conduct spatial differential expression between regions of interest.
Integrate additional omics (bulk RNA‑seq, proteomics, epigenomics) if desired.
